site.deck: Jessica Xie studies Communication & Multimedia Design at the Hogeschool van Amsterdam. Interfaces, exhibitions, editorial and graphic design, MUA work, and the photographs she takes along the way.
site.about_short: I have a background in communication and multimedia design, increasingly focused on UX/UI and visual design, fashion-informed art direction and user experience. My practice is shaped by curiosity and informed by culture, lifestyle, and the many ways creativity appears in everyday life.
about_long: I have a background in communication and multimedia design, increasingly focused on UX/UI and visual design, fashion-informed art direction, and user experience.

My practice is shaped by curiosity and informed by culture, lifestyle, and the many ways creativity appears in everyday life. Influenced by fashion and contemporary visual culture, I approach projects with both aesthetic awareness and strategic intent.
Outside of my studies I like to learn with my hands: I follow creative workshops in flameworking, ring-making, ceramic painting, origami and ikebana and chahua flower arrangement.
I’m interested in creating digital experiences and visual work that invite interaction and form meaningful connections with people.

projects.title: Gisou
projects.subtitle: The Icon of Honey Glow
projects.label: UX/UI Design
meta: UX/UI design, visual design, responsive design, CRM
projects.lead: “The Icon of Honey Glow” is a premium e-commerce campaign concept created for Gisou, centred on the Honey Infused Hair Oil as the brand’s iconic hero product.
body: The project explored how editorial storytelling, luxury beauty aesthetics and conversion-focused digital design could be combined into a cohesive cross-channel campaign experience across desktop, mobile and CRM touchpoints.

The homepage was structured as a narrative journey, moving from emotional campaign storytelling toward product discovery, ritual-based merchandising and community-focused conversion moments. Inspired by Gisou’s honey-infused identity and Mirsalehi heritage, the visual direction focused on warm neutral tones, spacious layouts, strong hierarchy and premium editorial imagery.
Alongside the responsive landing page, a complementary CRM email concept was developed to extend the campaign into a realistic luxury beauty e-commerce ecosystem.
This project allowed me to explore the intersection between branding, responsive UX/UI design, digital merchandising and campaign storytelling within a commercial e-commerce context.

projects.title: Gisou Retail
projects.subtitle: In-store concept
projects.label: Graphic Design
projects.lead: “Winter Honey Rescue” is a retail experience concept for Gisou’s Sephora Beauty Hub and EDG environments, centred on the Honey Gloss Ceramide Therapy Hair Mask as the hero product.
body: The concept explores how campaign storytelling, product merchandising and spatial branding can create a cohesive luxury beauty experience in-store. The visual direction is warm light in cold weather: Gisou’s signature honey tones and soft creams, with a subtle winter blue as a seasonal cue for hydration.

For the Beauty Hub, the focus is service and education. A lifestyle panel tells the product story in short paragraphs aligned with the French Sephora guidelines, the tester tray guides customers through a three-step routine (cleanse, repair, seal), and the service menu repeats that routine with a clear call to action: “Essayez le rituel”.

For the EDG shelf, I designed a “try first, buy next” flow: testers on the top shelf with a “Try me” call-out, the mask and hair oil as the “repair + seal” pairing in the middle, and the wider Gisou universe below. The background visual explains why the mask works: ceramides, hyaluronic acid and Mirsalehi Honey.
All campaign artwork, layouts and retail execution decisions are my own; AI-generated product mockups were used only to visualise the concept in context.

projects.title: Herinnering aan Tafel
projects.subtitle: Memories at the table
projects.label: UX Design
meta: UX research, service design, concept development
projects.lead: Developed over a six-month collaboration with Wereldmuseum Amsterdam, this project explores how immersive, sensory experiences can communicate stories of cultures under pressure.
body: Grounded in research and service design, the concept uses food as an entry point to connect visitors with personal narratives, cultural identity and collective memory.

Through a combination of storytelling, audiovisual elements and tactile interaction, the exhibition invites visitors to move beyond passive observation and engage with culture in a more embodied and reflective way.
